Role Overview

We are seeking a senior growth leader to own the full customer lifecycle – acquisition, onboarding, engagement, and retention – for a SaaS business exceeding $10M ARR. You will write the growth plan, control the budget, and be accountable for the results. This is a hands‑on role with real spend, a small specialist team, and authority to decide the next experiments.

Responsibilities

  • Growth Plan & Execution: Own the quarterly growth plan, set targets across acquisition, onboarding, engagement, and retention, and ship the work.
  • End‑to‑End Metrics: Own sign‑ups, activation rate, free‑to‑paid conversion, cohort retention, churn, expansion revenue, and CAC payback.
  • Acquisition: Lead organic, paid, product‑led, AI search, and marketplace channels; allocate budget each quarter.
  • Onboarding: Optimize the path from install to live consent banner, reduce drop‑off, deliver first value quickly.
  • Engagement: Build lifecycle programs via email, in‑app messaging, and product prompts to deepen usage.

About the Role

This role sits between our legal reality and our readers. CookieYes publishes a large library of privacy content that businesses across the world rely on to understand what the law asks of them, and we need someone professionally qualified to stand behind it.

We are looking for a law graduate who writes because they want to, not because a brief demanded it. You will track privacy legislation across jurisdictions, translate it into content our customers can act on, and act as the internal check on the legal accuracy of everything we publish and ship. Part of the role is genuine legal work: reviewing our own agreements, supporting compliance queries from customers, and keeping our product claims defensible.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor privacy and data‑protection developments globally, including GDPR, ePrivacy, CCPA, other US state laws, LGPD, PIPEDA, PDPA and emerging regulations; flag what matters for CookieYes and our customers.
  • Write authoritative long‑form content: regulation explainers, jurisdiction guides, compliance checklists, legal update posts and whitepapers.
  • Act as the legal‑accuracy reviewer for marketing and product content, adhering to an agreed turnaround SLA so reviews never stall the pipeline. Nothing that makes a compliance claim should ship without your reading.
  • Structure content for AI search, AI Overviews and answer engines, collaborating with the SEO and AI search team on generative‑engine optimisation, schema and citation‑worthy formatting.
  • Translate regulatory obligations into product requirements, working with product and engineering on how consent, records and disclosures need to behave.
  • Support customer‑facing compliance queries escalated by sales and support, and build internal reference material that reduces escalation frequency.
  • Review and maintain our own legal documents, including the privacy policy, terms of service, DPAs and vendor agreements, with external counsel where required.
  • Prepare briefing notes for leadership when a regulatory change affects roadmap or positioning.
  • Represent CookieYes’s point of view publicly through bylined articles, webinars and industry commentary.

Requirements

  • LLB or equivalent law degree from a recognised institution. Enrolment with a bar council is welcome but not required.
  • 2+ years of relevant experience in a law firm, in‑house legal team, compliance function or legal publishing role.
  • Demonstrable writing ability outside pleadings and contracts (publish work, blog, newsletter, or substantial piece for a non‑lawyer audience).
  • The instinct to write for a business owner rather than a bench; accuracy without legalese.
  • Working familiarity with data‑protection law, or clear evidence you can master a regulatory area quickly and thoroughly.
  • Fluency with AI tools for research, drafting and summarisation, paired with discipline to verify every citation, holding and date against the primary source before it reaches a draft.
  • Research discipline: cite primary sources, check whether guidance has been superseded, and avoid building arguments on secondary summaries.
  • Sound judgement about the line between explaining the law and giving legal advice, and care to keep our content on the right side of it.

Good to Have

  • A privacy certification such as CIPP/E, CIPP/US or CIPM, or intent to pursue one (support provided).
  • Prior experience at a SaaS, privacy‑tech or legal‑tech company.
  • Experience drafting or negotiating DPAs and SaaS agreements.
  • Comfort with SEO, GEO and how legal content performs in traditional search, AI search and AI Overviews.
  • Additional language ability relevant to EU jurisdictions.
  • Good understanding of, or familiarity with, major global privacy and data‑protection laws, including GDPR, CCPA, DPA, PDPA, UCPA and related regulations.

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Lead Performance Engineer with strong expertise in application performance engineering, production troubleshooting, and performance optimization. The candidate will collaborate closely with application development, DevOps, infrastructure, and database teams to identify bottlenecks, conduct root‑cause analysis, and drive performance improvements across enterprise applications.

Required Experience

  • 8+ Years of overall IT experience, with significant experience in Performance Engineering / Application Performance Management.
  • Proven experience troubleshooting complex performance issues in enterprise applications.
  • Strong understanding of JVM internals, memory management, threading, GC, CPU and I/O behavior.
  • Strong Linux troubleshooting skills.
  • Ability to independently perform performance analysis and identify root causes rather than only execute predefined test scripts.
  • Experience working with development, DevOps, infrastructure, and database teams.

Responsibilities

  • Lead end‑to‑end application performance engineering and troubleshooting activities.
  • Analyze application and server performance issues across development, test, and production environments.
  • Perform detailed Linux system‑level performance analysis (CPU, memory, disk I/O, network, processes, resource utilization).
  • Analyze JVM heap dumps to identify memory leaks, excessive object creation, and memory‑related bottlenecks.
  • Analyze thread dumps to identify deadlocks, thread contention, blocked/waiting threads, thread‑pool issues, and CPU‑consuming threads.
  • Conduct Garbage Collection (GC) analysis, including logs, pause times, heap utilization, allocation patterns, and JVM tuning opportunities.
  • Perform database performance analysis (slow queries, execution plans, connection pools, locks, waits, indexing, resource utilization).
  • Generate and analyze flame graphs to pinpoint CPU hotspots and application‑level bottlenecks.
  • Use application and server‑side monitoring/observability tools to detect performance degradation and correlate metrics across layers.
  • Conduct root‑cause analysis of performance incidents and provide actionable recommendations.
  • Work with development teams to identify inefficient code paths, resource utilization issues, memory problems, and concurrency‑related bottlenecks.
  • Define performance baselines and monitor application performance against agreed SLAs/SLOs.
  • Lead performance optimization initiatives and validate improvements through benchmarking and load testing.
  • Prepare technical performance reports, bottleneck analyses, and optimization recommendations.
  • Mentor junior performance engineers and provide technical leadership across performance engineering initiatives.

Key Skills & Technologies

  • JVM performance tuning, heap & thread dump analysis
  • Linux system performance diagnostics
  • Performance analysis tools (flame graphs, monitoring/observability platforms)
  • Database performance profiling and optimization
summary: Lead performance engineer to drive end‑to‑end application performance optimization across enterprise systems. Requires 8+ years IT experience and deep JVM/Linux expertise.
